source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Within what period should a physician countersign a telephone order?
questions.rationale: Telephone orders are countersigned by the ordering physician within the prescribed time, usually 24 hours.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Telephone Orders (PDF p. 9)
questions.quote: countersigned by the physician who made the order within the prescribed period of time (within 24 hours)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Who is the PRIMARY source of assessment data?
questions.rationale: The client is the primary source; family, records, and other professionals are secondary.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Assessment (PDF p. 9)
questions.quote: Client (primary)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In an emergency, which interview approach is used?
questions.rationale: The directive interview is structured with closed questions and is used in emergencies to get specific data.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Interviewing (PDF p. 10)
questions.quote: Used in emergency situation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which stage of the interview is MOST important for building rapport?
questions.rationale: The opening is the most important stage; it establishes rapport and orients the client.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stages of Interview (PDF p. 10)
questions.quote: Most important

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Checking a client's hydration status every 15 minutes is which type of assessment?
questions.rationale: Problem-focused assessment determines the status of a specific problem, such as hydration every 15 minutes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Assessment (PDF p. 10)
questions.quote: Hydration status every 15 minutes

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A home nurse compares a client's status now with data from 6 months ago. Which assessment is this?
questions.rationale: Time-lapsed assessment is done months after the initial one to compare with baseline.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Assessment (PDF p. 10)
questions.quote: Done several months after initial assessment

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Double-checking data to confirm accuracy is called:
questions.rationale: Validating is verifying data to confirm it is accurate and factual.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Validating Data (PDF p. 10)
questions.quote: Double checking or verifying data to confirm that it is accurate and factual

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which nursing diagnosis is written in the 3-part PES format?
questions.rationale: PES includes the problem, etiology, and signs/symptoms ('as manifested by').
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Diagnosis (PDF p. 11)
questions.quote: Basic 3-part statements (PES format)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A problem is not present, but risk factors make it likely. Which diagnosis type is this?
questions.rationale: A risk diagnosis is a judgment that a problem is likely to develop unless nurses intervene.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Nursing Diagnosis (PDF p. 11)
questions.quote: the presence of risk factors indicates that a problem is likely to develop unless nurses intervene

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: 'Readiness for enhanced family coping' is which type of nursing diagnosis?
questions.rationale: Wellness diagnoses describe readiness for enhancement.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Nursing Diagnosis (PDF p. 11)
questions.quote: Readiness for enhanced family coping

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: How should collaborative problems be labeled?
questions.rationale: Collaborative problems begin with 'Potential complications', e.g., PC: increased ICP.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nursing Diagnosis (PDF p. 11)
questions.quote: all collaborative problems begin with diagnosing label “Potential Complications”

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: To be useful for evaluation, how should goals be written?
questions.rationale: Goals are stated in behavioral, measurable terms (SMART) and involve the client and family.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Planning (PDF p. 11)
questions.quote: it should be stated in BEHAVIORAL TERMS

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: When does discharge planning begin?
questions.rationale: Discharge planning begins at first client contact with ongoing assessment of needs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Discharge Planning (PDF p. 12)
questions.quote: Begins at first client contact

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: What should the nurse do just before implementing an intervention?
questions.rationale: Implementation includes reassessing the client before an intervention.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Implementation (PDF p. 12)
questions.quote: Reassessing the client before implementing an intervention

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Evaluation done at or just before discharge to see if goals were met is:
questions.rationale: Terminal or summative evaluation determines whether goals are met, partially met, or unmet.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Evaluation (PDF p. 13)
questions.quote: Done at or immediately before discharge

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In Becker's Health Belief Model, which is an individual perception?
questions.rationale: Individual perceptions include perceived susceptibility, seriousness, and threat; age, peers, and media are modifying factors or cues.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Health Belief Model (PDF p. 13)
questions.quote: Perceive seriousness of an illness

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In Smith's models, defining health as the ability to perform one's work is the:
questions.rationale: Role performance model defines health by ability to perform work; eudemonistic is self-actualization.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Smith's Model of Health (PDF p. 13)
questions.quote: Role performance model — health is identified in terms of individual's ability to perform his/her work

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Travis's illness-wellness continuum moves toward high-level wellness through which steps?
questions.rationale: Movement right of the neutral point occurs through awareness, education, and growth.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Travis's Continuum (PDF p. 13)
questions.quote: Awareness

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A client stays home from work, and family confirms he is ill. Which stage of illness is this?
questions.rationale: In assuming the sick role, the person accepts illness and is excused from usual duties, with confirmation from family.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stages of Illness (PDF p. 14)
questions.quote: Excused from normal duties and role expectations

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Physical therapy after a stroke is which level of prevention (Leavell and Clark)?
questions.rationale: Tertiary prevention halts disease progression and rehabilitates, such as PT after CVA or speech therapy after laryngectomy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Levels of Prevention (PDF p. 15)
questions.quote: Physical therapy after CVA

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Getting married is which type of stressor?
questions.rationale: Situational stressors are unpredictable and may be positive or negative, such as marriage, divorce, or birth.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sources of Stress (PDF p. 15)
questions.quote: Situational stressors – are unpredictable and may occur at any time during life

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: In Selye's GAS, the 'fight or flight' release of epinephrine and cortisol occurs in which phase?
questions.rationale: In the shock phase of the alarm reaction, the ANS releases epinephrine and cortisone for fight or flight.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, General Adaptation Syndrome (PDF p. 15)
questions.quote: “Fight or Flight”

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: In which GAS stage does the body adapt and move back toward homeostasis?
questions.rationale: In resistance, the body adapts, limits the stressor, and moves back to homeostasis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, General Adaptation Syndrome (PDF p. 15)
questions.quote: Is when the body’s adaptation takes place

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Inflammation localized to an injured finger is an example of:
questions.rationale: In LAS, a person responds to stress through a particular body part or organ.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Local Adaptation Syndrome (PDF p. 15)
questions.quote: Man may respond to stress through a particular body part or body organ
